newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Generale says won't block Suez-Lyonnaise merger.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Generale says won't block Suez-Lyonnaise merger.

text.p: French conglomerate Generale des Eaux on Wednesday denied it planned to block a possible merger of Compagnie de Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux by launching a counter-bid for Suez.

But a spokesman said Generale chairman Jean-Marie Messier wanted a good price for the company's indirect stake in Suez, in the form of either a special dividend or a buy-out of Suez minority shareholders.

Both Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux declined any comment on Wednesday, consistent with their policy of keeping mum until after key board meeting in early April on the proposed merger that would create France's ninth largest company with a combined market capitalisation of 79 billion francs ($13.9 billion).

The Suez board is meeting from 1400 GMT on April 1, to discuss the 1996 annual results which will be published the following day. Suez chairman Gerard Mestrallet is expected to unveil the details of the merger plan at this meeting.
Lyonnaise's board is meeting on April 2.
Claude Bebear, chairman of insurance group Axa-UAP which has stakes in both Suez and Lyonnaise, also had no comment on Wednesday on a possible merger.
Asked by reporters during a news conference on the insurer's 1996 results whether he planned to play a role in the matter, Bebear replied: "No role".
"It is up to them to do what they want and we will take our decision as a consequence of that," he said.

A merger between Lyonnaise and Suez, reportedly first discussed two years ago but delayed due to property problems at both companies, would combine the cash-rich financial holding company Suez with Lyonnaise's ambitions and industrial activities, creating France's ninth biggest company in terms of market value.
Messier's firm holds an indirect stake in Suez through its 20 percent stake in Belgium's Electrabel and is the main domestic rival to Lyonnaise in water distribution and purification.

Speaking to reporters on Tuesday during a visit to a construction site in Lisbon, Messier said it was out of the question that his company would submit a counter bid for Suez, according to the Les Echos newspaper.
The La Tribune newspaper quoted him as saying, "The answer to whether Generale plans a counter-bid for Suez is clearly no. That has never been planned in whatever form."

"It is necesary to reduce the gap (between market price and asset value) of the stake in Suez in the event of an alliance, enabling the shareholders to share in the fruits of Gerard Mestrallet's work," Messier was quoted as saying by Les Echos.
Suez shares were trading 1.92 percent higher at 286.40 francs at 1122 GMT on Wednesday while Lyonnaise was 0.35 percent lower at 570 francs.
Both firms' shares have risen sharply in recent days as merger speculation has mounted.

Suez earlier this week took a dip because the market was expecting a takeover to take the form of a bid by the financial holding company for Lyonnaise in order to preserve significant tax receivables.
Analysts, comparing the relative market values of the two companies, arrived at a share swap parity of two Suez shares for one Lyonnaise.

But Le Monde newspaper on Tuesday and Les Echos on Wednesday said tat the bid was more likely to become an offer by Lyonnaise des Eaux for Suez. This would be because Lyonnaise would have to renegotiate many of its water contracts if it were to be taken over by Suez or anyone else, they said.
On the other hand, if the Finance Ministry gave its consent, Lyonnaise might still be able to use the Suez tax receivables.

A Lyonnaise bid for Suez, however, is raising some worries in Belgium where Suez, through its 62 percent stake in Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB), controls Tractebel, Belgium's main electricity supplier.
($ = 5.683 French Francs)
